revision.text:
{{Book | image = A-Guide-to-the-Astral-Plane-cover.jpg | caption = | code = TSR2625 | title = A Guide to the Astral Plane | author = [[Monte Cook]] | editor = [[Miranda Horner]] | cover_artist = [[Robh Ruppel]] | inter_artist = [[Adam Rex]], [[Jason Behnke]], [[Tony DiTerlizzi]] | cartography = [[Dennis Kauth]], [[Robert Lazzaretti]] | typography = [[Angelika Lokotz]] | publisher = [[TSR, Inc.]] | released = October 1996 | reprinted = | type = Accessory | binding = | pages = 96 | languages = | realm year = | game_edition = 2 | isbn10 = 0786904380 | isbn13 = 978-0786904389 | series = | preceded_by = | followed_by = | source = | Roll20number = 17287 }} '''''A Guide to the Astral Plane''''' is a 2{{nd}}-edition ''Advanced Dungeons & Dragons'' accessory. It is part of the ''Planescape'' campaign setting.
{{Quote|''Most berks think the Astral Plane's an empty place, serving as nothing but a cosmic highway connecting all the other places in the multiverse. Canny planewalkers know differently, though. Here are just a few of the 'secrets' of the Silver Void that this book explains:'' * ''It is the backdrop of the multiverse, where phenomena such as space and time are so vastly different from 'normal' that only a true blood knows his way around.'' * ''When he's on the Astral Plane, a basher moves, fights, and acts solely with his mind.'' * ''It is the closest thing the multiverse has to a 'plane of magic,' where sorcery and spells are not only more powerful, but are palpable, tangible objects.'' * ''The primary inhabitants are the infamous githyanki, an ancient race of wizards and warriors who know the dark of many secrets forbidden to others.'' * ''The Astral Plane is literally the dead-book of the gods.''}}
==Description== The book explains rules for astral travel, zero-gravity combat and spellcasting in the [[Astral Plane]]. It also provides information on the [[Githyanki]], the indigenous species on the Astral, which is suggested as an optional player species. The final section of the guide deals with other creatures that live on the plane, and describes a few locations.
==Contents== * All The World's A Stage: Introduction * The Space Between: Astral Space and Time * Racing Through Nothing: Astral Movement * Mindwar: Astral Combat * Spellwarp: Astral Magic * Mind Over Matter: Proficiencies * The Spiritweb: Conduits * Holes in the Fabric: Color Pools * Forgotten Husks: Dead gods * Mindstorms: Psychic Winds * The Githyanki * Creatures of the Void: Other Astral Inhabitants * Locations in Nowhere: Specific Astral Encounters

revision.text:
{{Book | image = A-Players-Primer-to-the-Outlands-cover.jpg | caption = | code = TSR2610 | title = A Player's Primer to the Outlands | author = [[Jeff Grubb]] | editor = [[Ray Vallese]] | cover_artist = [[Robh Ruppel]] | inter_artist = [[Tony DiTerlizzi]] | cartography = [[Robert Lazzaretti]] | typography = [[Angelika Lokotz]] | publisher = [[TSR, Inc.]] | released = May [[1995]] | reprinted = | type = Boxed Set | binding = | pages = 32 | languages = | realm year = | game_edition = 2 | isbn10 = 0786901217 | isbn13 = 978-0786901210 | series = | preceded_by = [[Fires of Dis]] | followed_by = [[In the Cage: A Guide to Sigil]] | source = | Roll20number = 17301 }} '''''A Player's Primer to the Outlands''''' is a 2{{nd}}-edition ''Advanced Dungeons & Dragons'' boxed set. It is part of the ''Planescape'' campaign setting.
{{Quote|''You've never seen a skull like this one, cutter - it's made of a silvery metal, with rainbow hues cascading over its shiny surface. Local bashers call it a mimir. Toss it into the air, and ask it questions: What is Ecstasy? Do fiends patrol the Outlands? The floating skull slicks softly, scouring its enchanted vaults for the answers. Then its bone-box opens, drivens by ancient pistons, and it begins to speak....''
''A PLANESCAPE accessory for player characters of all levels, the Player's Primer provides a look at the Outlands, which surround the great city of Sigil - the gateway to all the Outer Planes. In this box, a cutter'll find:''
* ''An audio compact disc that represents the mimir, a new magical item offering a strange and thrilling tour of the Outlands. More than 40 CD tracks allow players to hear what their characters would hear when consulting this handy (and some say dangerous) oracle.'' * ''A 32-page guide to the most important sites and features of the Outlands.'' *''A full-color poster map of the Outlands with never-before-seen maps of gate-towns.''}}
==Description== ''A Player's Primer to the Outlands'' is a boxed set containing a 32-page book written by [[Jeff Grubb]], a full-color poster map by [[Robert Lazzaretti]], and an audio CD.
''A Player's Primer to the Outlands'' is a guide to the [[Outlands]]--those areas surrounding [[Sigil]]--including descriptions of the locations and inhabitants of the Outlands. The interactive audio CD contains 41 tracks of Mimir interaction.
==Contents== * Welcome to the Outlands * Using the Booklet * Using the CD * A Word of Warning * The Mimir * An Overview of the Outlands * Moving through the Outlands * Magic in the Outlands * A Tour of the Outlands

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Automata

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Automata'' is the third track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Automata is the gate to the plane of [[Mechanus]], the plane of ultimate order. The members of the [[Council of Anarchy]] were tracked down, and a discussion of theirs was secretly recorded by me. A small portion of it follows: : '''[[Leggis Scrog]]''': Now remember: when the berk with the mimir comes by here, we pretend we're the [[Council of Order]], so we lure more leatherheads to this stupid town. No slip-ups this time, right, Ravis? : '''[[Ravis Corcuncewl]]''': Pike it, Leggis. You were the sod who slipped up last time. : '''Leggis Scrog''': And how do you figure that? : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': You and your stinkin' accent. Puttin' on the '''oh, I'm so holier than thou''' act that you practically fell over your own soddin' tongue. : '''Leggis Scrog''': Paugh! What a bunch of wash. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Help me out here, Aurach. : '''[[Aurach|Aurach the Fair]]''': Right, Ravis. Don't try to put the blame where it don't belong, Leggis. And both of you remember your parts. Not like last time, right? : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Got that, Leggis? : '''Leggis Scrog''': ''(grumbles)'' : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Shapeshift, Aurach, he's coming! : '''Leggis Scrog''': Greetings, honored one! : '''Mimir Agent''': How d'you do. : '''Leggis Scrog''': Welcome to our fair city. My name is Captain [[Arstimis]], and these are my fellow Councilors: [[Pelnis]] the Clockmaker... : '''Aurach the Fair, Mimir Agent''': (simultaneously) Hello. : '''Leggis Scrog''': ... and [[Serafil]], priestess of [[Lei Kung]]. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': How'd you do? : '''Mimir Agent''': Nice to meet you. : '''Leggis Scrog''': Now I understand that you desired a small description of our city for your master. : '''Mimir Agent''': Ha, indeed! : '''Aurach the Fair''': (aside to Ravis) Pompous windbag. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': (laughs, quickly covers it up with coughing) Excuse me. : '''Mimir Agent''': S'quite all right. : '''Aurach the Fair''': I am Pelnis, and I'm proud to make your acquaintance. : '''Mimir Agent''': Nice to meet you. : '''Leggis Scrog''': (aside to Ravis) That was close, I thought she'd forgot to shapechange. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Let me formally introduce myself. I'm Serafil of Lei Kung... : '''Mimir Agent''': Lovely. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': ... and it falls to me to tell you about our town. First I would like to stress exactly how easy it is to pass through the gate to [[Mechanus]]. : '''Mimir Agent''': Ah. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': There are a few ''minor'' forms... : '''Leggis Scrog''': (aside to Aurach) A few thousand! : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': ...So that we can ease the traffic through the gate and ensure proper placement in Mechanus. : '''Mimir Agent''': Excellent. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Our town is quiet, but there are many exciting features here. If a body's a merchant, we like him to come in with a fat purse — : '''Mimir Agent''': ... what? : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': I mean, a full load of goods, and ''leave'' with a fat purse. : '''Mimir Agent''': Wha... uh... I? : '''Leggis Scrog''': Well, you blew this one all by yourself, Ravis. Hey, berk. We're the Council of Anarchy. : '''Mimir Agent''': You—! : '''Leggis Scrog''': And we've just scragged our peel for your precious mimir. : '''Mimir Agent''': How dare you! : '''Leggis Scrog''': Oh, now, don't try to run! : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': Make with the dagger, Leggis! : '''Mimir Agent''': (sounds of a scuffle, a cry of pain, the thud of a body hitting the floor) : '''Aurach the Fair''': That's just great. We go to all that trouble and you two drop it like a [[tanar'ri]] baby. Now we've got to start all over. Hand me that mimir and we'll destroy it. : '''Ravis Corcuncewl''': I'd like to, but I'm afraid it's dissolvin' away. : '''Leggis Scrog''': Looks like it's time to change our identities. Again. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y3gR0_RfOpc This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Bariaur Tribes

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Bariaur Tribes'' is the 33rd track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': [[Bariaur]], the goat-men of the [[Outer Planes]], have long had tribes roaming around the [[Outlands]]. They are [[planar]] gypsies, never keeping to one place. They bring items to trade, and offer tests of skill. They also provide aid, if it is asked for; and opinions, even if they are not asked for. It has been said that what one tribe knows, the rest soon know, and so it is good advice for travelers to stay on a bariaur's good side. : For more information on these tribes, ask them directly. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=3537E_IyEsU This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Bedlam

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
The gate to Pandemonium is hidden away in a town called Bedlam. Part of the Outlands not oft visited by anyone in their right mind. To tell us about Bedlam, is Nicholas Silvar.
[Nicholas Silvar]
Damn this wind! Why won't it stop whistling in my ears!? Powers above! It's driving me crazy! Oh, wait. There it goes. Ah, who are you? Oh, right. Sorry. Sorry if I'm acting a little strange. It's just this wind, is all. Bedlam? That's all you want? You sure? Sure. Right. Then here's the chant. It's built on the body of a god that tried to escape from the howling land. The plane of winds. You can see his hand right over there thrusting out from the ground. Word has it, that if you look at his face from the sky, you can see his face grimacing against the ground, like he's still straining to get free. Matter of fact, right now we're sitting right on his nose, hehehe. I hate to be him. I haven't had a bath in weeks! Ahahahah! You don't suppose he knows who we are? Sorry, it was just a joke. You are a laughing kind of god, right? Probably not considering where you are. Oh well, it doesn't matter anyway. So, Bedlam 's run by a total flapping old bird. A wizard who can't cast a spell to save his life. Or so it seems. He's smarter than the rest of us combined. Comes from studying Pandemonium too much, hahaha!. One day I'll do him in and then I'll be the ruler here. Unless the god comes through. Of course if he did, he'll probably just get tumbled, sliced, and scragged, hehe, before he realized where he was. That's what sort of town this is. Hey, don't you get too close to me or I’ll nick you? I will. Ah! You're too close! (punching sounds, screams).

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Curst

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
The Gate to Carceri is surrounded by the town of Curst, a five-ringed walled city. It's filled with those who can't stomach the thought of others in power. Bitter revolutionaries who seek revenge on the universe, that didn't treat them as they expected. The walls are covered in razor vine, and the guards of the town are instructed to let anyone in. It's getting out, that's the problem. A nameless local of Curst speaks of her town.
[Nameless Local Female]
Get that thing out of my face (punch sounds)! You want to know about Curst? I'll tell you about it, sod. It's the best place there is!. That is, if you're rich and have power. Otherwise, it's one of the most miserable places in the planes. Everyone here 'ates everyone else, and there's too much ??? going on for berks to control their tempers. It's a bloody mess, it is, and I'm not just saying that as a figure of speech. I mean it literally. Real blood, real mess. Works like this. Everybody plots against everybody else. Plots usually end in bloodshed, between the plotters most often. They just can't seem to get along with each other, or anyone else most often. So, 'at's Curst for you. Now buy me the drink I promised, or I'll make you sorry you ever talked to me in our first place.

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Dwarven Mountain

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
High in the mountains of the Outlands lies a triple realm, shared by three Dwarven Powers. The rocky peaks outside hold the trading town of Iron Ridge. Inside and underneath sit the Realms. The three dwarven powers are: Vergadain, god of luck, Dugmaren the Smith, and Dumathoin, master of minds. Vergadain's proxy, Lazuli Clearfacet, was kind enough to speak for us.
[Lazuli Clearfacet]
(coughs) So, you want to come to the dwarven mountains, eh? (coughs) Well, bring your money and your luck, because you're going to need both (coughs, wheezing). The place where I work, Strong Gale (wheezing), the realm of Vergadain (wheezing), is a place of drinking and gambling, but unless you're invited (wheezing) you're probably not too welcome, cheaters especially (wheezing). Anyone who comes here to peel honest gamblers will see that we mean (wheezing) business when it comes to...
[Male 1]
Hey! That berk's using loaded dice!
[Lazuli Clearfacet]
(coughs) Excuse me...
[Male 1]
Told you about the loaded dice
[Lazuli Clearfacet]
What have we here? A cheating human? Loaded dice?! Let me see those. (Let's see those) Seven (seven!). And seven again (seven!) Seven once more. This bodes ill for you, friend.
[Male 2]
Look! Look!
[Male 3]
I swear! These were the dice at the table when I got here!
[Male 4]
How come I didn't roll those sevens?!
[Male 3]
Just unlucky.
[Male 4]
Unlucky?! I'll show you unlucky!
[Lazuli Clearfacet]
Take this berk out and execute him! He knew the rules when he came here!
[Male 3]
Please have mercy! I was framed!
[Male 5]
Bash him!

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Ecstasy

revision.text:
['''Mimir'''] Ecstasy is a gate-town to Elysium, the plane of utter goodness. This is Barathorn Maddison, a member of a Transcendent Order
[Nameless Male 1]
Hey, berk! Get out of the middle of the street! [Barathorn Maddison]
Get one thing straight. I believe in action before thought. In training the body so much, it's always a step ahead of the mind. I also believe that Ecstasy is virtually perfect. Well, maybe virtually isn't the word to use. Anyway, it really gets up my nose that the philosophers' court is located in this town. What's the point of action without thought? The other day I heard a bunch of old philosophers arguing about how many baatezu it takes to put a torch in a ceset.
[Nameless Male 2]
None! My asked to see the way you draw see ya
(note I couldn’t hear this segment well 0:47 of the track I did my best this ia rough draft though)
[Nameless Female]
Or all of them want to put it in and the rest to claim credit for it.
[Barathorn Maddison]
See? See? Everyone's a wise guy, everyone's got an answer.
[Nameless Male 3]
one side
[Barathorn Maddison]
Worse, there's nothing physical about arguments here. I mean, there's still arguments, they're philosophers for crying out loud, but there's no violence in the court. A body's wit had better be sharper than her sword, for a well chosen word can decimate a foe better than a sword thrust.
[Nameless Male 4]
<nowiki>*</nowiki>crying*
[Nameless Female2]
What happened?
[Nameless Male 4]
He used sarcasm...
[Barathorn Maddison]
That's why I hate it. I hate thinking about things! I figure, just do it! Hey, that's a catchy phrase...

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Excelsior

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
Excelsior, the gate-town to mount Celestia- naturally attracts those who tend toward the tenants of Law and Good. This is the Gessare, Sarah La Siva
(couldn’t understand the name so I know its butchered)
[Gessare, Sarah La Siva]
I traveled to Excelsior from Chals, hoping it would shake the dust of strangeness from my eyes. Unfortunately, the two places were so different and I had trouble getting used to life in this berg. After I did, I started making my keep near the forum and brought Mimir with me to capture any valuable darks the paladins might let slip. I went to that place for days on end, and finally decided to get this piece of a speech captured on the Mimir. The speech is exactly the same as every other speech I heard, only with different words. There was no difference in content.
[Random Paladin Speach]
Brethren! We have come here to share in each other knowledge, to write our own names in the book of glory and chivalry (absolutely right!). Yet we accomplish nothing by standing around speechifying (yeah, yeah!). We could be out addressing evil, smiting the foes of Law and Goodness where they stand. It is our duty, nay, our right to destroy our enemies. Our codes demand the destruction of these foes, yet we remain safely in Excelsior, while our antagonists grow stronger. Let us ride out my brothers and sisters! (continues in the background)...
[Gessare, Sarah La Siva]
The next speaker said approximately the same thing, and likewise the next after that. The only time it got interesting was when two paladins of a rival church nearly came to blows over their definitions of Law. I'm sure it's the same now as it was then, and it'll probably be the same when I go back, in about 20 years

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Faunel

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
Faunel's gate leads to the Beastlands. It's a ruined city, always teetering on the brink of destruction. To tell us of Faunel, is TOS to Sher, a zebra-striped cat centaur from an unknown location.
[TOS to Sher a Ze]
The beauty of Faunel is that anyone partial to animals is welcome here. If you don't mind holding a conversation with an animal that's probably smarter than you are, purr, you'll get along fine. It's said that people come here to forget their past lives, to lose themselves in the dreaming nights and glorious ruins of Faunel. Tn fact that's where I met my mate. I was stalking dinner in some fascinating ruins that I'd never explored before, and he was doing the same. Except that he wasn't sure I was sentient, so he was hunting me. When we got that straightened out, we became fast friends. We still fight like sharks and dolphins but there's always love and trust there. We went to Rath, the ruler of Faunel, to get his official sanction to our union. I'll probably get killed by the vile hunt for saying this,hmm but I don't really give a meow. The way I figure it, anything with a loving heart and some intelligence is good enough for me. That's what I look for in a mate. I don't care if it's green, purple, or pink bi- or quadrupedal human, or feline. As long as it's a loving soul. That's what I look for.

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Fortitude

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
Arcadia’s gate-town is Fortitude, also called the Egg. One of the main buildings of Fortitude is the confessional. It is a wide, ???-like amphitheater with perfect acoustics. The residents come here to admit their faults, and to let their fellow citizens pass judgment on them. All abide by the decisions of the many.
Okay. Okay, okay, okay, come on, quiet down, quiet down, please come on. My turn! Come on, listen. I got to confess a sin. (what?) All right, here it is: I hate all this honesty . There it is, that's my crime, simple yet hideously complex. Please forgive me, listen, I hate this town. (what?) Are you listening? Listen, hey buddy! Hey, same to you. Bring your cow home later. I hate Fortitude! There it is, that's the crux of the matter. I can't lie here or else I'll be punished. you know what I mean? Listen, there's no diplomacy or tact here. I can't tell someone who's exceptionally large like, like, hey you! Hey, big butt. See? I can't say "You're big-boned". I mean. come on. I can't feign interest in someone like you, buddy, just cuz I want to get at your money. You know what I'm saying? Come on, people. I can't try to get rid of someone by saying "See you later", when I have no intention of ever seeing you again, you ugly berk! (laughs) You know what I mean? Come on, I'll be publicly flogged! Go on, get out of here! Listen, people, I want to live in a place where a body's always worried about crime, you know what I mean? I mean, I want to be able to lie, and have that to be the least of the things you have to look out for! You know what I'm saying! I mean, wacky, but, I hate law and order! (laughs) I don't want to be regulated and looked over. You know why? I'll tell you why! I love being insecure! There it is! What a horrible place this is! Yeah, don't you think so? Love these wacky audiences! See ya!

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Gate-towns

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Gate-towns'' is the second track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Scattered along the rim of the [[Outlands]] are the [[gate-town]]s: burgs that have grow up at the spots along the [[Great Road]] that branch off into the other [[Outer Planes]]. All of the Outer Planes have a gate-town associated with them. : Speaking of gate-towns is the noted sage, [[Ariana Arachnis]]: : '''Ariana Arachnis''': There are sixteen gate-towns that lead to the Outer Planes. By gate-town, I mean a town that has grown up ''around'' the gates, a natural point on a trade route. The towns are usually populated by those who find the plane beyond to their liking. The towns all possess a character much like the associated plane, but there's always something that keeps the town from [[Cosmic realignment|sliding]] over into the next plane; by this, I mean that there are elements that are drawn to the town simply because they want to become too much like its plane, keeping the town Outlands. I trust this is perfectly clear. : Alphabetically, the towns are: [[Automata]], leading to [[Mechanus]]; [[Bedlam]], leading to [[Pandemonium]]; [[Curst]], leading to [[Carceri]]; [[Ecstasy]], leading to [[Elysium]]; [[Excelsior]], leading to [[Mount Celestia]]; [[Faunel]], leading to the [[Beastlands]]; [[Fortitude]], leading to [[Arcadia]]; [[Glorium]], leading to [[Ysgard]]; [[Hopeless]], leading to the [[Hades|Gray Waste]]; [[Plague-Mort]], leading to the [[Abyss]]; [[Ribcage]], leading to [[Baator]]; [[Rigus]], leading to [[Acheron]]; [[Sylvania]], leading to [[Arborea]]; [[Torch]], leading to [[Gehenna]]; [[Tradegate]], leading to [[Bytopia]]; and [[Xaos]], leading to [[Limbo]]. : Now, any questions? == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GHXVPqCwbvY This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Glorium

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Glorium'' is the 10th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': The town of [[Glorium]] watches over the gate to [[Ysgard (plane)|Ysgard]], and the people watch over the town, though they deny caring about anything that much. [[Flatnose Grim]], a ranger who's got the town loyal to him, speaks of Glorium: : '''Flatnose Grim''': If you've gotta come here for business, get your business done, and get out, period. We don't much like outsiders, so don't expect sweetness and light from us, eh? If you're going to move here, come prepared to work and work hard. We all pull our own weight here, and there's no reason why ''you'' should be an exception. Now, if you're coming here to seek the wisdom of [[Odin]] or any of the other [[power]]s, stick around. You'll learn more by dealing with us than by prostrating yourself on some temple floor. If you've got the secret of the universe and you wanna tell us, ''do it''! If we don't like it, we'll ''pound'' you, but we'll do it friendly-like, just to let you know we disagree. And if you can't handle that, then you ''really'' don't belong here. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=6KpbrPakdHY This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Gzemnid's Realm

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Gzemnid's Realm'' is the 25th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Tangled in with the lowest levels of the [[Dwarven Mountain]] and [[Ilsensine]]'s [[Caverns of Thought]] is the [[Gzemnid's Realm|realm]] of [[Gzemnid]], the [[beholder]] god. All mimir agents who entered the realms never emerged again. : '''Mimir Agent''': No. No. No! Not that! Anything but that! No! page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Hopeless

revision.text:
['''Mimir''']
The gate to the Gray Waste is wrapped around by the city of Hopeless. The gate itself is a pool of a black, viscous, tar-like substance through which those who want to travel to the Gray Waste must jump. This is Klobby One-Hand.
[Klobby one hand]
Sure. I can tell you about Hopeless. There's probably no point to it, but I'll do it because there's nothing else to do. First off, you'll want to take off that blue cloak before you go any further into town, unless of course you feel like having it confiscated by berks whose eyes can't stand any color but gray. Now let's see... what can I say about this place? Huh, the people ain't got no individuality, they're all sort of shocked-looking, wandering through life like there's no point to the whole thing. That's probably true, but on the other hand I'm new here. Already told you about the "no color" thing. Hmm? Now the people here are pretty dullard bunch, and they can work up a huge mess of hatred that spills out like puss from a lanced boil when it suits them. Usually they don't, though, because they've got their feeling stripped away from them. What else? Oh yeah, if you've got the chance, catch Thingol the Mocking's next piece of art. I hear it's called "Child and Boulder". I don't know what happens, but Thingol got this thing for grotesque art. So it should be pretty good

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Indep Villages

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Indep Villages'' is the 35th track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Not every place in the Outlands is so fiercely contested as the gate-towns. Take, for instance, the Indep Villages, as described by [[Mara Gulajal]], a resident of a hidden village in the fourth ring. : '''Mara Gulajal''': Hey, berk. Sit at home and enjoy your experiences there. We don't want you leatherheads coming through here like you own the place. We make our own lives here, see? We don't want no trouble. We're peaceful and friendly... to each other, and everyone else can go pike themselves, right? : Now, I know I seem unfriendly, but if you'd see the things we have, you'd feel the same way. Rotting plague-walkers. [[Walking castle]]s. Fiend patrols. Herds of [[bariaur]] stampeding! Lizard-men! ''Armies marching right outside our door''! : You'll forgive us if we don't slaughter the fatted calf every time one of you barmy adventurers comes through! == Background Information == == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=R0vifK1a31g This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" |- | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''

page.title: A Player's Primer to the Outlands/Ironridge

revision.text:
[[File:A Player's Primer to the Outlands CD.jpg|300px|right]] ''Ironridge'' is the 23rd track on the audio CD portion of '''[[A Player's Primer to the Outlands]]'''. == Transcript == : '''Mimir''': Perched on the outer crust of the [[Dwarven Mountain]], [[Ironridge]] is a community of bashers who decided to try their hands at dealing with the dwarves. This is [[Key Nilscar]], a trader, gambler, and jack-of-all-trades. : '''Key Nilscar''': Ironridge is an ideal place to jump off and hit three realms. It's only about a day away from [[Gzemnid's Realm]], the [[Caverns of Thought]], and even less from the Dwarven Mountain. I originally came here to see if I could get a shipment of dwarven weapons and iron to some friends of mine in [[Rigus]]. But I couldn't cut a deal, and I'm not being paid anywhere near enough to try and waylay a dwarf caravan. Though I probably could if I had half a mind to.'' : Anyway, when the Rigus deal fell through, I figured I'd stick around and do some gaming in the Mountain. If I could just wangle an invite, I'll show those sods a thing or two about dice! I've heard they execute cheaters, so I guess I'll just have to be a little extra careful, eh? Heh. : If you're coming to Ironridge, ''have a reason''! People here don't like layabouts any more than dwarves do. == External Links == [https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=MkdZTLzdsHY This track on YouTube] {| class="fandom-table browser" style="width:100%" | class="prev"|'''Previous Track'''
